title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles became immobilized during Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco when traffic gridlock prevented movement long enough to fully drain their batteries. At least a dozen vehicles were stranded on city streets, requiring some to be towed away. The system was deployed into conditions—major unplanned traffic disruptions and road closures during a high-volume event—that exhausted a resource it depends on to function.

A battery management system that cannot sustain idling through predictable urban congestion, or a deployment decision that did not account for how major public events degrade traffic flow, would have caught this failure before vehicles were abandoned on streets. One vehicle also caught fire after driving over fireworks debris, showing the system's vulnerability to hazards introduced by crowds. It is not established whether the battery drain alone would have prevented movement or whether traffic conditions made any movement impossible.

The deployment exposed a gap between the operating conditions Waymo's vehicles were designed for and the actual variability of San Francisco streets during major events. City officials and the company indicated they would work to prevent similar incidents, but the concrete changes needed remain unspecified.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic. Video footage verified by NBC News showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, many of them Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets following fireworks displays, with some requiring towing assistance. The company attributed the gridlock to major traffic disruptions, high volumes of travelers, and unplanned road closures. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks that someone had set off in the street, though no injuries were reported.

The incident prompted city officials and Waymo to evaluate the situation. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to have conversations with public and private partners about improving traffic management for future events. Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to strengthen its resilience during major traffic disruptions. This situation echoes a previous incident in December when a power outage caused some Waymo vehicles to malfunction at intersections with nonworking traffic lights. The city's Department of Emergency Management has emphasized the need for better coordination to prevent similar delays in the future.
